lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

Are you currently responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with him and are you responsible for his care and upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me actually. But I do help support him financially - I contribute towards his upkeep regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

Who does Alex live with, and are you paying towards his upkeep as part of a formal arrangement or voluntarily?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum. I pay towards his upkeep - I help with things like clothes, food, and other bits he needs. It's a regular thing I do to support him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. 

To clarify further - are you paying child maintenance through the Child Maintenance Service (CMS), or through a court order, or is this an informal arrangement where you're contributing directly?

Also, I need to ask: Is Alex's mum claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's an informal arrangement - I just contribute directly to help with his costs. And no, his mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just to confirm - you mentioned you contribute towards Alex's upkeep by helping with clothes, food, and other necessities on a regular basis. Can you tell me approximately how much you contribute per week towards his upkeep, and is this contribution at least equal to the Child Benefit rate (which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute about £26 a week towards his upkeep - so just over that amount.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail.

Now I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Are you and Alex both currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK. I live here and Alex lives here too with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A few more questions:

1. Are you or Alex subject to immigration control, or do either of you have any restrictions on your right to reside in the UK?

2. Is there anyone else who might also be contributing towards Alex's upkeep at a similar or higher rate than you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us has any immigration restrictions - we're both here without any issues like that. And no, I'm the main one contributing towards Alex's upkeep financially.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions:

1. Do you have a National Insurance number?

2. Is Alex in full-time non-advanced education or approved training? (I ask this to confirm the standard rules apply for his age - at 8 years old, he would normally qualify as a child for Child Benefit purposes.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have a National Insurance number. And Alex is 8, so he's just in primary school - normal school for his age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While you are contributing financially to Alex's upkeep at a rate that exceeds the Child Benefit amount (£26 per week), the key issue is that Alex lives with his mother. Under Child Benefit rules, **priority for claiming goes to the person the child lives with**. 

Even though Alex's mum is not currently claiming Child Benefit, she would have the priority to make a claim as the person Alex lives with and who is responsible for his day-to-day care. Since Alex doesn't live with you, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

If Alex's mother wanted to claim Child Benefit, she would be the one who should apply. Is there anything else I can help clarify about this?

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, which meets the age requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant and Alex both live in the UK with no immigration restrictions, and the claimant has a National Insurance number. However, Alex does not live with the claimant - he lives with his mother. The claimant contributes approximately £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep through an informal arrangement, which exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child. While contributing towards a child's upkeep can qualify someone for Child Benefit when the child doesn't live with them, this generally applies when the child lives with no one else (such as being away at boarding school) or in specific circumstances. In this case, Alex lives with his mother, who is not claiming Child Benefit. Under Child Benefit rules, priority for claiming goes to the person the child lives with. Since the claimant does not live with Alex, and Alex lives with his mother, the claimant would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. The mother would have priority to make a claim as the person Alex lives with and who is responsible for him.
